chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Ash'ari, who said:

Some of my paternal uncles wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What do you say regarding a young girl whom her paternal uncle married off, but when she grew up, she refused the marriage?' He wrote in his own hand: 'She is not compelled to accept it, and the matter is hers (her choice).'
ai.seo_question: Does a woman have the right to reject a marriage arranged by her guardian upon reaching maturity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the status of the paternal uncle (al-'amm) as a valid guardian (wali) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing his authority from the father's. Imam al-Jawad’s response establishes the principle of 'Khayr al-Niqah' (the right of option) for the mature girl, confirming that her consent is not merely a formality but a substantive condition for the marriage's validity. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the woman's agency in marital contracts, contrasting with some Sunni schools where the guardian's decision may be binding.
